correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md (Git blob 0faf225e618bf6f36892420b4de51c04f09922c7) treats F(x,y)=(alpha cos x+beta x sin(pi y),y+x) on the entire real plane, alpha,beta>0. A genuine two-cycle has first coordinates u,-u (u>0), and midpoint z satisfying alpha cos u=beta u cos(pi z) sin(pi u/2), 1=-beta sin(pi z) cos(pi u/2). The second equation excludes beta<1, and beta=1 requires u=2k and cos(2k)=0, impossible by irrationality of pi. For beta>1 the reduced scalar resonance equation (2n±t)Phi_beta(t)=alpha|cos(2n±t)| has Phi_beta(0)=0, Phi_beta'(0)=pi sqrt(beta^2-1)/2>0. Uniform derivative domination gives one root on each side of 2n for every large n; reconstruction of (cos pi z,sin pi z) prevents extraneous roots. A uniform Lipschitz estimate gives the stated O(n^-2) location remainder even for small |cos 2n|. Independently solved and checked 12 high-precision full orbit returns for beta=1.82,1.05. No global census outside two small windows is proved.
residual_risks: The proof excludes only primitive period two for beta<=1 and gives two remote local branches per sufficiently large n for beta>1; no assertions on stability, all finite amplitude cycles, or higher periods.
